For a given element in LTE the relative population of two excitation levels is given by the Boltzmann formula  

  N₂ / N₁ = (g₂ / g₁) exp[ – ΔE / (k T) ]

where  
ΔE = E₂ – E₁ (in energy units) and k is Boltzmann’s constant.  
Because g₂ / g₁ is a constant, the change of the level–population ratio between two temperatures depends only on the exponential term:

  (N₂ / N₁)_hot / (N₂ / N₁)_cool = exp[ –ΔE/k (1/T_hot – 1/T_cool) ]

1. Transition energy  
The line has λ ≈ 1448 Å = 1.448 × 10⁻⁷ m.  
ΔE = h c / λ  
  = (6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J s)(3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) / 1.448 × 10⁻⁷ m  
  ≈ 1.37 × 10⁻¹⁸ J  
Convert to eV: ΔE ≈ (1.37 × 10⁻¹⁸ J)/(1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ J eV⁻¹) ≈ 8.6 eV.

2. Compute ΔE / k  
k = 8.617 × 10⁻⁵ eV K⁻¹ → ΔE/k ≈ 8.6 eV / 8.617 × 10⁻⁵ eV K⁻¹ ≈ 9.9 × 10⁴ K.

3. Temperatures  
No–spot photosphere: T_hot = 6000 K  
Spotted photosphere (effective): T_cool = 5500 K

4. Population–ratio factor  
1/T_hot – 1/T_cool = 1/6000 – 1/5500  
  = (5500 – 6000)/(6000 × 5500)  
  = –500 / 3.3 × 10⁷  
  ≈ –1.515 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹

Hence  

factor = exp[ –ΔE/k (1/T_hot – 1/T_cool) ]  
  = exp[ –(9.9 × 10⁴ K)(–1.515 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹) ]  
  ≈ exp(1.50) ≈ 4.5.

Thus the level-population ratio (level 2 / level 1) in the no-spot case is about 4.5 times larger than when 40 % of the surface is spotted—consistent with the observed decrease.

The closest option is:

(D) ~4.5

Answer: D
